newsitem.title: USA: Insured loss from U.S storms estimated at $280 mln.
newsitem.headline: Insured loss from U.S storms estimated at $280 mln.

text.p: A series of violent storms that struck the U.S. West Coast in late December through early January caused an estimated $280 million in insured property damage, an insurance industry trade group said.
Property Claim Services, an industry supported organization that tracks insurance losses, said the preliminary estimate includes only damage covered by private insurance.
The estimate does not include flood damage, which is insured under programs administed by the federal government, PCS said.
PCS said it expects insurers will handle over 180,000 claims related to the storms, which caused damage in Washington, Oregon, California, Idaho and Nevada.
"While the proportion of total damage covered by the private market is not large, the volume of claims to be handled by insurers is significant," PCS assistant vice president Gary Kerney said.
Most of the insured property damage was caused by strong winds, snow and ice and heavy rains from the storms, which hit in the periods December 26 to 27 and December 28 to January 1, PCS said.
The strong winds toppled trees onto power lines, causing power outages, and onto structures, vehicles and other insured property.
The weight of ice and snow collapsed roofs and other structures. Heavy rains damaged the interiors of structures and vehicles.
Problems were compounded by mild temperatures and heavy rains, which accelerated the melting of the snow, resulting in widespread flooding.
Disaster declarations were issued in all five states.
